name: Straight leg raise
movement: both legs straight, one lifted to thirty to forty five degrees and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you. Shoulders to feet have to be in the picture.

words.hint: Lying on your back, one straight leg lifted fifteen to forty five degrees, the other knee bent or straight.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your back side on to it, one leg straight, the other bent or straight.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone, the working leg straight on the floor, toes pulled up. Bend the other knee with the foot flat if your back prefers it; it can stay straight. Shoulders to feet in the picture.
words.top: One straight leg lifted fifteen to forty five degrees off the floor, knee locked, toes up, the other foot still on the floor.
howto: Lie on your back. Bend the other knee with the foot flat on the floor — or keep it straight if that is comfortable. Pull the toes of the working foot toward you.
Tighten the thigh so the knee is locked straight, then lift the whole leg until the heel is about a ruler's length off the floor — never past forty five degrees, the height of the other knee.
Hold at the top for five seconds, knee straight, toes up, the other foot on the floor.
Lower slowly, keeping the knee straight, until the heel is back on the floor. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: Whether the lower back is flat on the floor, the leg rolling out, and whether the thigh is truly tight: it sees the knee angle, the lift, the toes and the other foot. Press the back down yourself.
words.about: Straight leg raise — lying on your back side on, the working leg straight, the other knee bent with the foot flat or straight: the lift, as the change in the angle at the hip between the shoulder and the knee since the start, 15–45° at the top (leaflets give the heel 10–20 cm off the floor; 45° is the height of a bent knee); the lifted knee at least 165° so the leg stays straight; the other heel kept down, whether that leg is straight or bent; and the foot's angle at the heel, 60–105°, toes pulled up. The knee and the toes are coached before the lift is asked for. Hold five seconds at the top, lower over two, and the rep counts when the heel is down. The working leg is the straight one lifted: a bent knee sits higher but is not the one measured.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, feet to shoulders in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the lower back or the front of the hip pinches. Bend the other knee with the foot flat — it keeps the back flat.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold; no weight.
words.harder: A longer hold; an ankle weight; slower lowering.
words.mistakes: The knee bending on the way up; lifting past forty five; swinging the leg up; toes pointing away; the other leg lifting; the back arching.

measurements.label: knee straight

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee kept straight: 180 is locked out. Below the band it is bending.

measurements.label: leg lift

settings.label: Lift at the top, at least (degrees)
Lift at the top, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: How far the working leg has lifted: the angle at the hip between the shoulder and the knee, as its change from rest (which follows a resting leg that settles), turned so a lift reads up. 0 with the leg on the floor, 45 lifted forty five. Read from the working leg alone, so the other knee may be straight or bent with the foot flat; shoulders to feet have to be seen. Also the progress measurement.

measurements.label: other foot down

settings.label: Other heel lifted, at most (% of the shin)

measurements.why: The other heel's height, as its change since the start, as a share of that shin: it stays on the floor whether that leg is straight or bent with the foot flat. Optional: when the model cannot see it the lift is still read.

measurements.label: working leg
measurements.why: Not judged: it picks the working leg. The hip's bend less the knee's bend — about 45 for a straight leg lifted forty five, 0 for a straight leg on the floor, below 0 for a knee bent with the foot flat — so the straight lifted leg is measured even though a bent knee sits higher.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee
measurements.why: The foot against the shin, at the heel: it grows as the toes point away. Toes pulled up keeps the quad working and the knee straight.

faults.label: Knee bending
faults.text: Straighten your knee — tighten the thigh
faults.deep: Lock the knee straight before you lift

faults.label: Toes pointing away
faults.text: Pull your toes up toward you
faults.deep: Toes up — pull the foot back toward you

faults.label: Other leg lifting
faults.text: Keep the other foot on the floor
faults.deep: The other leg is coming up — press it down

faults.label: Too high
faults.text: Not so high — forty five degrees at most
faults.deep: Lower it — no higher than the other knee

faults.label: Lift short
faults.deep: Higher — the heel about a ruler's length off the floor

settings.label: Lift that counts as under way (degrees)
